topics.label: Lecture introduction: Initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by outlining the lecture's focus on deepening knowledge of known immune cells and molecules during inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Principles of innate recognition: PAMPs, DAMPs, and PRRs
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the fundamental mechanisms of innate recognition, including the nature of PAMPs and DAMPs, criteria for pathogen targets, and receptor localization.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptor families, signaling, and the inflammasome
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major families of pattern recognition receptors, their intracellular signaling cascades, and the assembly of the inflammasome to produce inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Sentinel cell activation and leukocyte recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tissue sentinel cells detect infection and coordinate the multi-step recruitment and extravasation of circulating leukocytes to the inflammatory site.

topics.label: Lymphatic drainage and adaptive immune priming
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how dendritic cells carry antigens through lymphatic vessels to lymph nodes to activate adaptive immune responses.

topics.label: Pathophysiology and clinical severity of septic shock
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the lethal systemic consequences that arise when massive, uncontrolled pro-inflammatory cytokine production triggers widespread vasodilation and organ failure.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how acute inflammation is terminated, how damaged tissue is repaired, and how persistent stimuli lead to chronic inflammation or granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next lecture preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the presentation and announces the topic of the upcoming lecture.
